# Elbow dislocation

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Trauma and orthopedic surgery > Upper extremity > Elbow dislocation*

[Original Article Link](/library/0l0evT)

---

## Summary

<u>Elbow</u> <u>dislocation</u> is an atypical separation of the radial, ulnar, and humeral <u>joint</u> surfaces. A <u>posterior</u> <u>dislocation</u> of the <u>elbow</u> is common and is typically caused by a <u>fall on an outstretched hand</u>. Clinical features include <u>pain</u>, swelling, visible deformity, and reduced active <u>range of motion</u> of the <u>joint</u>. An <u>elbow</u> <u>dislocation</u> is classified as complex if there is an associated <u>fracture</u>. Diagnosis is confirmed with <u>radiography</u>. <u>Elbow</u> <u>dislocations</u> without an associated <u>fracture</u> are <u>managed conservatively</u> with <u>closed reduction</u> and <u>immobilization</u>. Complex <u>elbow</u> <u>dislocations</u> require <u>surgery</u> with <u>open reduction and internal fixation</u>. Complications of <u>elbow</u> <u>dislocation</u> include nerve injury, <u>brachial artery</u> injury, <u>joint</u> instability, and posttraumatic stiffness.




See “<u>Radial head subluxation</u>” for information on partial <u>dislocation</u> of the <u>head of the radius</u> at the <u>radio-humeral joint</u>.
